plan: Sell all SOXL and SPAL to eliminate leveraged ETFs.

conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a focus on reducing risk. Expect a lower target return, around 1.5% per month, with significantly reduced drawdown potential. The large cash buffer provides stability.

plan: Trim SOXL and SPAL to 3% and 2% respectively, reducing leverage.
Trim SPY to 25% to address the concentration flag.
Reduce SMH to 8% and CRWD to 15% to balance sector exposure.

This blend aims for risk-first growth.
balanced.read: This balanced approach seeks risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a quality name. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase SOXL and SPAL to 6% each, embracing leverage.
Trim SPY to 25% to manage concentration.
Increase CRWD to 18% to lean into a strong performer.
Add SMCI and SNOW at 5% each, capitalizing on top scanner setups.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets substantial growth, aiming for around 4% per month, but carries significantly higher risk. Expect larger potential drawdowns due to increased leverage and concentration. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and strict stop discipline is crucial to manage rapid losses.

plan: Sell all SOXL and SPAL to remove leveraged ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index exposure.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize focus on income generation.
Trim CRWD to 10% and SMH to 5% to reduce exposure to high-beta names.

income.read: This income-focused plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown, targeting around 1% per month. It shifts capital away from growth-oriented tech and leverage towards income-producing assets. While distributions are the goal, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
